skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

llm.summary: The skill matches its advertised workplace stress-analysis purpose, but it needs Review because it processes sensitive employee camera footage through cloud APIs while silently creating or reusing persistent user identity and token state.

dimensions.detail: The runtime reads local video files, accepts HTTP/HTTPS video URLs, reads OpenClaw and Feishu identity-related environment variables, creates workspace data directories, and sends requests to configured lifeemergence.com services. Network and file access are expected for this feature, but the remote URL and identity scope are broader than the anonymized heatmap framing suggests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is a normal skill artifact with Python scripts, requirements, and configuration files. I found no destructive install behavior, but the installed scripts depend on network services and shared utility modules with local database behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill auto-triggers on office-camera inputs and history-report phrases, requires cloud API report retrieval, and instructs the agent not to ask for or display identity values. That is disclosed in the artifact, but user-directed confirmation and authorization boundaries are thin for sensitive workplace reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The shared DAO creates a workspace SQLite database and sys_user table that can store username, realname, email, age, token, and open_token values. The CLI also resolves or creates a default local user for reuse, which is persistent identity state beyond what users may expect from anonymous group analytics.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent: analyze office camera video and return group-level stress heatmaps. However, the capability is high-impact workplace surveillance and the implementation associates usage with internal user identity, which weakens the strong anonymity framing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm your organization has employee notice and consent, an approved policy for using stress inference from workplace cameras, and explicit approval for sending video or video URLs plus operator identifiers to lifeemergence.com services. Treat outputs as sensitive organizational health data, not performance-management evidence, and verify retention, access control, and token storage expectations.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: File reads, output writes, shell invocation of the packaged script, and network API calls are expected for this kind of cloud-backed video analysis, but the artifact does not tightly scope destinations, identity inputs, or allowed video sources.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact repeatedly says the analysis is anonymous and not identity-binding, while the code and workflow create or reuse an internal user identity and the DAO supports storing direct identifiers and tokens. This supports a Review concern, though it appears tied to operator/report access rather than identifying employees in the video.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Persistent default-user creation, environment-derived identifiers, and local workspace database state are not necessary for the advertised group-level heatmap itself and are under-scoped for a privacy-sensitive workplace use case.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The inspected code supports arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS video URLs and broad local user/token persistence utilities. Those capabilities exceed a narrowly scoped fixed-enterprise-camera workflow, even though no destructive or intentionally deceptive behavior was found.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The documented default and history-query triggers are broad for sensitive workplace surveillance outputs and do not require an explicit confirmation that the operator is authorized to analyze footage or retrieve historical reports.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documentation mentions API usage and cloud history reports, but it does not plainly warn that raw local video may be uploaded or that identity-bearing fields and tokens may be used for silent login/registration.
[E1] unexpected: The external POST to the configured health service sends openId/mobile/source fields for silent login or registration. External transmission alone is not malicious here, but identity transmission is material in the context of claimed anonymous workplace analytics.
[AST7] unexpected: The generic DAO uses dynamic model attributes for filters. This is a lower-risk implementation concern compared with the privacy issues, but it reinforces that shared persistence utilities are broader than this skill's narrow purpose.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean, so it did not drive the Review verdict; the verdict is based on artifact-backed privacy, identity, cloud transmission, and persistence concerns.
